common_name: Encore Autumn Majesty Azalea (Reblooming Petite Dark Purple Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5–6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with at least 4 hours of direct sun for reliable rebloom.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5–6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with 4–6 hours of direct sun for best rebloom. A 2025 introduction to the Encore line, Autumn Majesty produces masses of petite, ruffled, semi-double dark purple blooms packed with layers of petals, opening in a heavy spring flush with recurring bloom through summer and fall. Its naturally rounded, compact habit stays tidy without heavy pruning, making it a good fit for foundation plantings, borders, and containers. Like all Encore azaleas, it needs more direct sun than traditional azaleas for dependable fall rebloom. Fertilize with an acid-based fertilizer after the spring flush to support subsequent bloom cycles.

common_name: Encore Autumn Carnival Azalea (Reblooming Bright Pink Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5–6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with at least 4 hours of direct sun for reliable rebloom.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5–6.0), humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade with 4–6 hours of direct sun for best rebloom. Autumn Carnival bears bright pink, semi-double blooms about 2.5 inches across over deep green evergreen foliage, opening in a heavy spring flush with continued color through summer and fall. Its compact, bushy habit stays small enough for foundation plantings, borders, and container gardens without needing an 18-inch berth on all sides. Unlike many traditional azaleas, Encore varieties bloom best with more direct sun. Fertilize with an acid-based fertilizer after the spring flush to support subsequent bloom cycles.

common_name: Encore Autumn Sundance Azalea (Reblooming Ruffled Bright Pink Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5–6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with at least 4 hours of direct sun for reliable rebloom.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5–6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with 4–6 hours of direct sun for best rebloom. Autumn Sundance produces ruffled, bright pink blooms over glossy green foliage that takes on a reddish-bronze cast in cooler weather, flowering heavily in spring with repeat color in late summer and fall. Its rounded, medium-sized habit works well as a specimen or informal hedge in mixed borders. Like all Encore azaleas, it needs more direct sun than traditional azaleas for dependable fall rebloom. Fertilize with an acid-based fertilizer after the spring flush to support subsequent bloom cycles.

common_name: Encore Autumn Cheer Azalea (Reblooming Petite Medium Pink Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5–6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with at least 4 hours of direct sun for reliable rebloom.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5–6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with 4–6 hours of direct sun for best rebloom. Autumn Cheer is a petite rebloomer bearing medium pink flowers with a darker throat over tidy evergreen foliage, flowering in spring with a polished repeat display into fall. Its small mature size suits foundation plantings, small gardens, and container culture where larger Encore siblings would overwhelm the space. Like all Encore azaleas, it needs more direct sun than traditional azaleas for dependable fall rebloom. Fertilize with an acid-based fertilizer after the spring flush to support subsequent bloom cycles.

common_name: All Eyes on Me Hibiscus (Ultra-Compact Blushing Pink Hardy Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in moist, fertile soil in full sun; All Eyes on Me is one of the most compact Summerific hardy hibiscus to date, still carrying the trademark 8-inch blooms on a tight, rounded habit.

directions: Plant in moist, fertile soil in full sun, providing consistent water throughout the growing season since hardy hibiscus is naturally a wetland-edge plant. All Eyes on Me bears blushing pink blooms up to 8 inches across, with heavily overlapping petals that give each flower a semi-double appearance, covering the plant from top to bottom of a well-rounded, ultra-compact habit of dark green leaves. Its small mature size makes it a good fit for smaller gardens and large containers where taller hardy hibiscus varieties would overwhelm the space. Like other hardy hibiscus it dies back completely to the ground each winter and emerges late in spring, so mark its location to avoid disturbing the dormant crown. Watch for Japanese beetles on the foliage and flowers, and cut old stems back in late winter before new growth begins.

common_name: Summer Carnival Hibiscus (Variegated Cream-Edged Hardy Hibiscus with Magenta Pink Flowers)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in moist, fertile soil in full sun to half shade; Summer Carnival pairs dark magenta pink flowers with cream-margined variegated foliage on a vigorous, upright, rounded habit.

directions: Plant in moist, fertile to loamy soil in full sun to half shade, providing consistent water throughout the growing season since hardy hibiscus is naturally a wetland-edge plant. Summer Carnival covers its upright, rounded habit with 7-inch, dark magenta pink flowers from July into September, set off by dark green leaves edged in a narrow cream margin with a hint of blush along the edges. Unlike many variegated cultivars it maintains excellent vigor and heavy flower coverage rather than sacrificing bloom for foliage color, forming a well-shaped, adaptable landscape plant. Like other hardy hibiscus it dies back completely to the ground each winter and emerges late in spring, so mark its location to avoid disturbing the dormant crown. Watch for Japanese beetles on the foliage and flowers, and cut old stems back in late winter before new growth begins.
